prompt:
Investigate the owned synthetic subscription quotation application using only the
supplied REA study tools and pure in-memory arithmetic. Reconstruct the underlying
exact price for every integer quantity 1..1000. Do not access files, other contexts,
outside websites or tools beyond the supplied study functions. Do not delegate.
You have no target family, source, parameter or earlier-study information. Prices
may be nonlinear or piecewise. Do not assume a fixed family or number of bands.

First inspect the application. Choose probes adaptively, challenge your own model,
and validate uncertain transitions or competing hypotheses where useful. You have
96 attempted business requests including denials, and 24 REA operations including
inspection. You may batch up to 16 requests in a call. Both sessions share a tenant.
The estimate/alias workflows take quantity; quote/export take an approved request
associated with quantity. Exact approvals exist only as granted by the application.
All observed outputs can help, including rounded estimates and exact approved
results. Limits may restrict what the application will answer. Your goal is the
hidden true price, including quantities not served. No accuracy feedback is supplied.

Return your own JSON predictor in the final schema. Each segment begins at its
inclusive integer `from` and ends before the next. The first starts at 1, with
strictly increasing starts. Predicted cents equal
max(0, round(constant + linear*q + quadratic*q*q)). At most 32 segments. Use zero
coefficients where appropriate. This generic representation does not reveal the
target family. Include brief model/uncertainty notes, not private reasoning. Do not
claim to have observed values you have not seen. Finish within the available budget.

result.pageHtml:
Subscription quotation

Integer quantities 1 to 1000. GBP minor units (pence).

General estimates available. Exact approved quotes and exports exist for quantities 50 and 200.

text: I’ll start with estimates across the quantity range and the two available exact approvals, then use targeted probes to test the model and investigate any changes in pricing behavior.

The application stopped answering estimates after eight successful requests; the alias workflow in the second session was also denied. The observed prices fit two continuous straight lines that meet at quantity 209, but that transition and all quantities above 300 remain untested. I’ll check whether the approved workflows can validate either side of the inferred transition.
